interactions.summary: Jiang closes the alchemy aside by saying the Comedy offers endless study from many angles even if he cannot personally decode all of it.
A Dante passage is read on greediness, the corruption of innocence, and the way human flourishing rots under endless downpour.

Jiang hears the passage as pitying human short-sightedness, a student asks whether it is a call for peace amid Italian turmoil, and Jiang rejects that frame in favor of enlightenment through expanded imagination and cosmic sight.
The next English tercet on moral corruption is read, followed by the same lines in Italian.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Participants reading Dante in English and Italian

interactions.summary: Jiang briefly moves the class onward after the paired readings.

claims.claim: Jiang says the Divine Comedy offers a lifetime of study because it can be approached from many angles even where he cannot fully decode a given layer.
The quoted passage presents greediness as a force that pulls mortals downward and corrupts the good blossoming of human will.
Jiang hears the tone of the greed passage as sadness and pity from a higher vantage, where Dante and Beatrice can see how humans fight over trivial things and abandon spiritual pleasures.
A student asks whether the lament should be read as Dante's call for Italians to stop fighting and unite toward peace and understanding.
Jiang rejects the peace-reading and says Dante is instead calling for recognition of the cosmos's infiniteness through expanded imagination and sight.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang relocates Dante and Beatrice above the world, pitying humans for trading higher spiritual pleasure for nearly nothing.
signature_moments.source_phrase: humans insist on fighting for almost nothing in our world
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This keeps the packet's moral altitude and the contrast between petty struggle and enlarged spiritual sight.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang dismisses the political peace frame and makes the sharper demand: asking for peace is useless unless imagination itself expands.
signature_moments.source_phrase: Asking for peace does you no good
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the packet's cleanest Jiang reversal from moral wishfulness to transformation of perception.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's preferred frame for Dante's call: not social peace first, but expansion into the vastness of the cosmos.
